title: AI-First Customer Success Showcase
summary: A DevRev PLuG + Turing AI showcase environment for prospects evaluating DevRev as an AI-native support platform. Demonstrates: AI-deflection on common questions via PLuG, Turing-powered ticket triage and auto-routing, AI-generated KB article suggestions, sentiment-based escalation, and the full omnichannel loop (email, chat, Slack). Designed for a modern SaaS company ('Velo Analytics') with a realistic product hierarchy and a mix of low-complexity deflectable tickets and high-severity escalations that show what the AI escalates vs. handles autonomously.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Prerequisites — verify before running setup steps
steps: Confirm the DevRev user behind your PAT has the Admin role. Builder/Member roles cannot reach all Settings menus, and several integrations require Admin to install snap-ins.
Confirm the PAT itself was generated by that same Admin user. PATs inherit the creator's role at the moment they were issued — escalating the user later does NOT re-scope existing tokens.
If a step below returns an 'access required' or HTTP 403 error, regenerate the PAT from an Admin account and rerun `dia doctor` before retrying.
Some Settings menus are scoped per-workspace; confirm you're operating in the workspace the customer will use, not your default DevRev org.

ui_guidance_sections.title: PLuG AI widget — what to demo first
steps: Open the PLuG widget in the demo org and ask: 'How do I share a dashboard?' — AI instantly cites the KB article and resolves without human.
Then ask: 'My entire data pipeline is down and I've lost two hours of data' — AI detects the severity and escalates immediately. Show the contrast.
Then express frustration: 'This is the third time this month my pipeline has broken' — Turing flags negative sentiment and triggers the CSM alert. Show the timeline_entry AI annotation on the ticket.
This three-step flow — deflect, escalate, sentiment — is the core of the AI-first story in 5 minutes.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configuring the PLuG AI agent
steps: Go to Settings → PLuG → AI Agent to view and edit the grounding notes in this blueprint.
The ai_grounding_notes field tells Turing what the product is, who the users are, what to answer, and critically — what NOT to answer (billing, pricing, contract terms).
Connect KB articles to the AI agent under Settings → PLuG → Knowledge Base. Published articles in this blueprint are automatically eligible for AI grounding.
Test grounding quality using the Preview mode before going live.
Adjust tone, fallback behavior, and human handoff triggers under Settings → PLuG → Escalation Rules.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Turing AI triage — auto-routing and summarization
steps: Turing automatically classifies every incoming ticket by product area, priority, and intent — no manual tagging needed.
Routing rules are configured under Settings → AI → Triage. For this showcase, tickets with 'pipeline' or 'connector' keywords route to the Data Engineering Support group.
Billing questions route to Billing & Ops. Sentiment-negative tickets route to Customer Success.
Turing generates a 2-3 sentence summary on every ticket so human agents have instant context when they pick up an escalation.
Show the 'AI Triage Queue' group in the demo — every ticket that arrives here has been pre-classified and summarized before a human sees it.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Sentiment detection and churn-risk escalation
steps: Turing scores every message for sentiment. Scores below -0.7 trigger the 'sentiment-negative' tag and a CSM alert.
The 'churn-risk' tag is applied when: (a) sentiment is negative AND (b) the account has had 2+ P0/P1 tickets in the last 30 days.
Configure escalation rules under Settings → AI → Sentiment Escalation. Set the threshold, the team to notify, and the escalation message.
In the demo, show work:t08 (Lena Marchetti's frustration ticket) — the internal timeline entry shows the AI scoring and the automatic CSM notification firing within 90 seconds.
Emphasize: the CSM was notified before any human support agent even saw the ticket. This is proactive retention, not reactive firefighting.

ui_guidance_sections.title: AI-generated KB article suggestions
steps: When AI cannot fully resolve a ticket, it suggests the top 3 matching KB articles for the agent to review and share.
Agents can push a KB article directly to the customer from within the ticket — no copy-paste.
If the AI suggestion resolved the ticket, mark it 'AI Resolved' and tag it 'ai-suggested-article'. This feeds the deflection rate metric.
Use Settings → AI → Knowledge Gaps to see which tickets had no matching article — these are gaps in your KB that should be filled.
For the demo: show the AI article suggestion panel on work:t02 (Snowflake auth error) — the AI matched the re-authentication article at 0.94 confidence.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Custom stages for the AI workflow
steps: This blueprint adds four custom stages to complement DevRev's built-in pipeline.
'AI Handling' (ordinal 150) — ticket is being worked by the AI agent. No human has seen it yet.
'Awaiting User' (ordinal 350) — AI asked a clarifying question; waiting for the customer to respond.
'Escalated to Human' (ordinal 450) — AI determined it cannot resolve this and handed off to a human agent.
'AI Resolved' (closed, ordinal 750) — AI resolved the ticket autonomously. Tracked separately from human-resolved for deflection metrics.
Go to Settings → Object Customization → Stage Diagrams to configure the allowed transitions and set up automation rules that move tickets between AI Handling and Escalated to Human.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Measuring AI deflection rate
steps: Deflection rate = tickets tagged 'ai-deflected' / total tickets in period. Target: 60%+ for mature AI-grounded orgs.
Track in DevRev Insights: create a metric filtering tickets by the 'ai-deflected' tag and trending over time.
Mean time to resolution (MTTR) for AI-resolved tickets vs. human-resolved tickets shows the velocity improvement.
Knowledge Gap report (Settings → AI → Knowledge Gaps) shows which categories need more KB articles to improve deflection.
During the demo, show that deflection isn't just about cost savings — it's faster for the customer (seconds vs. hours) and frees human agents for the complex, high-value conversations.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure SLA policies
steps: Settings → SLA Policies → Create
Recreate each policy below, matching the priority targets exactly.
Policy: Enterprise AI-Enhanced SLA (applies to acct:northstar)
Notes: Enterprise SLA for Northstar — AI handles initial triage within 2 minutes; human first response guaranteed within 30 minutes for p0/p1.
First-response: p0 (blocker) ≤ 30m, p1 (high) ≤ 1h, p2 (medium) ≤ 4h, p3 (low) ≤ 24h
Resolution: p0 (blocker) ≤ 4h, p1 (high) ≤ 8h, p2 (medium) ≤ 48h, p3 (low) ≤ 120h
Policy: Standard AI-Assisted SLA
Notes: Standard SLA — AI deflection targets 60%+ of tickets. Human SLA clock starts only after AI handoff.
First-response: p0 (blocker) ≤ 1h, p1 (high) ≤ 2h, p2 (medium) ≤ 8h, p3 (low) ≤ 48h
Resolution: p0 (blocker) ≤ 8h, p1 (high) ≤ 24h, p2 (medium) ≤ 96h, p3 (low) ≤ 240h

ui_guidance_sections.title: Deploy the PLuG chat widget
steps: Settings → PLuG → Widget
Copy the JavaScript snippet and add it to your site's <head> (or deploy via GTM).
Set welcome message: "Hi there! I'm Velo's AI support assistant. Ask me anything — I can usually answer instantly. If not, I'll connect you with a human right away."
Set primary brand color: #6366f1
Enable the AI agent for L1 deflection.
Ground the AI on the KB articles seeded by this blueprint (Settings → AI Agent → Sources).

Notes: You are Velo Analytics' AI support assistant. Velo is a B2B SaaS analytics platform used by data teams. Users are typically data analysts, data engineers, or business intelligence managers. Common questions: connecting data sources, pipeline failures, dashboard sharing, billing/seat management, and API quota errors. Always check KB articles before escalating. For billing questions, route to the billing team. For data pipeline outages, escalate immediately to p0. Do not share internal pricing tiers or contractual information — route those to the sales team.
Enable fallback to ticket creation when the AI cannot resolve.

Customer-portal auth limitation: the customer-facing portal does NOT support federated login (SAML / OIDC). End users authenticate via email + magic-link only. Surface this early in the POV if the customer is expecting SSO for their end users.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure Slack integration
steps: Settings → Integrations → Slack
Click 'Connect Slack Workspace' and authorize DevRev in the OAuth flow.
Choose a default channel for ticket-event notifications.
Enable bidirectional sync between Slack threads and ticket timelines.
Set up the /devrev slash command for in-Slack ticket creation.
Constraints to flag with the customer up front:
- Only ONE public Slack connection per DevRev org. If they have multiple Slack workspaces, pick the one the support team uses for the POV.
- Enterprise Slack accounts require DevRev Support to whitelist the OAuth app before the install will succeed. File the request with Support ahead of the demo if the customer is on Enterprise Grid.

🤖 Turing AI: Matched KB article 'Sharing Dashboards — Public Links, Embeds, and Guest Access' (confidence: 0.94). Article shared with user via PLuG. User confirmed resolved. Ticket closed without human intervention. Deflection: ✓
